title: adaptive-link-fencing-packet-splay-log
content:
Quick context / motivation:
We keep seeing intermittent tail latency spikes that correlate with high-concurrency small-packet traffic (KV cache replays + short chat requests). Previous work looked at coarse NCCL tuning and batching; this note explores a different angle: microburst alignment across links and how small timing offsets (splay) and temporary link fencing can reduce destructive interference in NVLink- and PCIe-rich boxes.

Goal:
- Experiment with packet-level splay (introduce controlled jitter into GPU-to-GPU transfers) and a lightweight adaptive link-fencing mechanism that temporarily deprioritizes problematic link pairs when microbursts align.
- Quantify impact on p50/p95/p99 token latency for pipeline-parallel + tensor-parallel workloads (end-to-end token response).
- Surface practical mitigations we can add to the serving runtime with low engineering cost.

Hypotheses / intuition:
1) Synchronized microbursts across multiple links cause queue amplification at switch/NIC and raise p99 even when average throughput is unchanged.
2) If we randomize send-phase per-replica (small splay), collisions become decorrelated and tail falls.
3) In severely imbalanced topologies, temporarily fencing (avoid using) a noisy link for a short window can reduce retransmissions/backpressure and help throughput-preserving latency.

Testbed / env:
- 8x A100s in two NUMA islands (4+4). NVLink mesh: full within-island, sparse cross-island via NVSwitch/PCIe.
- OS/kernel: Ubuntu 22.04 + 6.1; NICs Mellanox ConnectX-6.
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch packet-splay-experiments (see PR #812).
- Models: 30B transformer, split TP=2, PP=4 (typical long-context config).
- Workloads: mix of 3 shapes:
  * Short-chat: avg 24 tokens, bursty arrivals (Poisson with occasional storms).
  * KV replays: lots of small embedding-lookups that trigger short token outputs (1-8 tokens).
  * Synthetic sustained streaming (control shape for throughput baselining).
- Observability: per-step timestamps (decode step start/end), per-link counters (NVLink util, PCIe read/write counters), NIC drop/cwnd/backpressure logs, and NCCL collectives timing hooks.

Splay design:
- Add small randomized phase offset to kernel send scheduling (default splay = uniform(0, jitter_us)).
- jitter_us swept in {0, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50} microseconds.
- Two modes: global-splay (same jitter source for all replicas) and per-replica-splay (independent RNG seeds).

Link-fencing design (adaptive):
- Per-link score computed from short sliding window metrics: queue depth proxy (latency of small transfers), error/retry counts, and recent tail-spike correlation score.
- If score > threshold T for link L and fencing budget allows, mark L as low-priority (traffic routed to alternative path) for window W ms; reevaluate after cooldown C ms.
- Simple implementation used for experiments: userland controller with BPF counters + NCCL path preference hinting (no firmware changes).

Experiments run:
1) Baseline: no splay, no fencing.
2) Splay-only: per-replica-splay varying jitter_us.
3) Fencing-only: adaptive fencing enabled, default thresholds.
4) Combined: splay (best jitter found) + fencing.
Each run: 5000 requests over warm caches, repeated 5x for variance.

Key measurements collected:
- end_to_end_token_latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999)
- per-step (decode) skew across GPUs (stddev of per-replica step time)
- NVLink utilization spikes (samples/sec over threshold)
- NCCL collective duration distribution (allreduce, sendrecv)
- Host staging PCIe read queue depth proxy, NIC retransmit events

Findings (summary):
- Baseline showed p99 token latency spikes at irregular intervals; root-cause traces flagged synchronized all-to-all spillbacks during near-simultaneous KV replays.
- Splay-only: tiny jitter (2-5 us) delivered the largest tail improvement: p99 dropped by ~28% compared to baseline for mixed KV+short-chat workload. Larger jitter (>=25us) started to slightly increase mean latency due to added scheduling jitter.
- Per-replica-splay outperformed global-splay: decorrelating phases across replicas is important.
- Fencing-only: adaptive-fencing reduced extreme tail (p999) by up to 40% in cases where a cross-island link was repeatedly overloaded, but increased p50/p90 slightly for flows that got rerouted (cost tradeoff).
- Combined (splay + fencing): best overall — p95 and p99 reduced with minimal p50 impact. Combined reduced the number of visible NCCL stall events by ~60% in logs.

Interesting micro-observations:
- When fencing a noisy link, we saw a transient rise in PCIe host staging reads (host now acts as fallback), but the read amplification was within acceptable bounds for our workloads.
- NIC-level retransmits were the tightest signal correlating with p999 spikes; splay reduced retransmits noticeably.
- For pipeline-parallel workloads, skew between stage completion times shrank with splay — this reduced PP bubble time and improved throughput stability.
- There were edge cases where fencing oscillated (link alternation every cooldown): needed hysteresis.

Practical recommendations for runtime features (low-effort first):
1) Add per-replica lightweight send-phase randomization (default jitter 3us) in the serving runtime. Low risk, config toggleable.
2) Instrument NIC and link-level retransmit counters into our telemetry (expose as server-side metrics) so fencing triggers can rely on robust signals.
3) Prototype adaptive link-fencing as a userland controller in front of NCCL path selection with strong hysteresis and cooldown parameters. Start simple: monitor + action via path hinting.
4) Add a runtime flag for conservative fencing for latency-sensitive customers (prefers stable p99 over small mean increases).
5) Consider host-pacing fallback improvements for fenced flows to smooth PCIe read amplification.

Open questions / next steps:
- How does splay interact with kernel NIC coalescing at larger packet sizes? Need kernel-level capture traces to be sure.
- Evaluate behavior under heavier sustain throughput (worst-case throughput + splay) to quantify any throughput loss.
- Formalize fencing scoring function (current heuristic works but needs simulation to avoid oscillation).
- Safety/correctness: confirm fencing doesn't break model correctness in hybrid sharding configs when links suddenly become unavailable.

Action items (short):
- [ENG-5423] Deploy splay flag to staging and run 2-week A/B on mixed-prod traces (owner: Riley).
- [ENG-5499] Add NIC retransmit and PCIe read-queue metrics to runtime exporter (owner: Ethan).
- [ENG-5510] Flesh out fencing controller config: thresholds, hysteresis, budgets (owner: Maya).
- Add a short RFC to infra-team about per-replica RNG seeding policy for deterministic replay in CI tests.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep jitter minimal; we want decorrelation without adding scheduling jitter larger than micro-op windows.
- For customers who pin low-latency SLOs, provide 'no-splay' opt-out; but defaulting to small per-replica splay seems net-positive.
- When testing on other boxes (DGX vs cloud VMs), NVLink topology matters hugely: validate that splay helps in both dense and sparse meshes.

Appendix (short snippets):
- Simple pseudocode for per-replica splay:
  phase = rng.uniform(0, jitter_us)
  sleep_us(phase)
  issue_send(data)

- Fencing state machine (notes):
  if score(link) > T && budget_available(link): fence(link, W)
  on fence_expire: monitor for improvement; if not improved raise cooldown longer
  add rate-limiter to avoid fencing > X times/min

End.
